title: Beat an egg in a pan with a whisk while holding the pan steady by its handle
instruction: Hold the pan steady by its handle and beat the egg in it with the whisk until the yolk and the white are mixed together. Touch the egg only with the whisk, and keep all of the egg in the pan and the pan flat on the burner.
context: Beating eggs is one of the commonest kitchen jobs: one hand steadies the pan while the other whisks until the yolk is broken up through the white. Sliding or tipping the pan moves the egg about but leaves the yolk whole.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A black glass-ceramic hob plate, 28 x 28 cm and 6 mm thick, fixed to the table with its centre 24 cm forward and 10 cm right of the centre line; on it, at the same centre, a grey burner ring 25 cm across. (2) A dark grey non-stick pan with straight sides, inside 20 cm across and 4.5 cm deep, 0.9 kg, loose, standing centred on the burner ring; its black handle (14 x 2.4 x 1.6 cm) points straight left toward the left arm, level, near the rim. (3) The egg: 101 wooden beads 10 mm across, 0.8 g each, in one layer on the pan's floor at the points of a 1.55 cm square grid centred on the pan's centre: 37 yellow beads (the yolk) on every grid point up to 5 cm from the centre, and 64 white beads (the white) on every grid point from 6 cm to 9.25 cm from it. (4) A stainless-steel balloon whisk, 14.2 cm long, 60 g: eight wires forming a bulb 5 cm across and 7 cm tall, a steel collar and a black handle 6 x 2.2 x 1.6 cm; it stands upright, wires down, in (5) a white ceramic whisk holder, a tube 5.3 cm across inside and 4.5 cm tall, fixed to the table with its centre 26 cm forward and 29 cm right of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Measured at the end of the trial from a photo from above, placing each bead by its centre. 0.0 if at any time the pan tilts 5 degrees or more (one edge about 2 cm up) or lifts more than 1 cm off the burner ring, or a gripper's fingers go into the pan below its rim (the egg may be touched only with the whisk), or if at the end the pan's centre is more than 3 cm from the ring's centre or more than three beads are outside the pan. Otherwise it depends on how far the yolk is broken up: two yellow beads belong to the same patch when their centres are less than 1.7 cm apart (a gap under 7 mm), linked through other yellow beads too. 1.0 if no patch holds more than 12 of the 37 yellow beads; 0.5 if the largest holds 13 to 24; 0.0 if it holds more (the yolk starts as one patch of 37, and moving the egg about whole keeps it one). The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with everything still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed: stand the pan back on the ring with its handle pointing left, lay the beads back on their grid points with a paper template (yellow up to 5 cm from the centre, white from 6 cm out), and stand the whisk back in its holder.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the egg is 101 rigid beads standing in for liquid, with damping in place of rolling resistance; the whisk's eight wires are straight 3 mm bars; the pan's round wall is 24 flat segments; the hob and ring are flat plates; friction is set (beads 0.25, pan 0.5, whisk 0.9); the cameras render at 320 x 176.
